name: Coorg (Kodagu)
description: Coorg is a hilly district in the Western Ghats known for its coffee and spice plantations, dense forests, and Kodava culture. It suits nature lovers and those seeking a quiet hill retreat, but expect heavy rain from June to September and weekend crowds from Bangalore year-round. Infrastructure outside Madikeri is limited, so a hired car is essential.
nearest_airport: Mysuru Airport (120 km) or Mangaluru International Airport (135 km)

attractions.name: Abbey Falls
attractions.description: A 70-foot waterfall on the Cauvery tributary, surrounded by coffee and spice plantations. The viewing platform is easy to reach but the falls are most impressive during and just after the monsoon; in summer they reduce to a trickle.

attractions.name: Raja's Seat
attractions.description: A small government-maintained garden on a hillock in Madikeri town, historically used by Kodagu kings to watch the sunset over the valleys. The view is genuinely good at dusk but the garden itself is unremarkable.

attractions.name: Madikeri Fort
attractions.description: An 18th-century fort built by Tipu Sultan and later modified by the British, now housing a museum and a church within its walls. The fort is modest in scale and the museum collection is thin, but it gives useful historical context for the region.

attractions.name: Namdroling Monastery (Golden Temple)
attractions.description: One of the largest Nyingma Tibetan Buddhist monasteries outside Tibet, located in the Tibetan settlement of Bylakuppe near Kushalnagar. The main prayer hall contains three massive gilded statues and is genuinely striking; the surrounding settlement has a calm, lived-in atmosphere.

attractions.name: Dubare Elephant Camp
attractions.description: A Karnataka Forest Department camp on the Cauvery river where elephants from the Mysuru royal stables are brought for the monsoon. Visitors can watch bathing and feeding sessions in the morning; the experience is brief and the site gets crowded on weekends.

attractions.name: Talacauvery
attractions.description: The sacred source of the Cauvery river at an elevation of about 1,276 m on Brahmagiri Hill, with a small temple tank and a steep 2 km trail to the hilltop offering wide views. The drive up is scenic through thick forest; the site has deep religious significance for Kodavas and receives heavy pilgrim traffic during Cauvery Sankramana.

attractions.name: Iruppu Falls
attractions.description: A tiered waterfall on the Lakshmana Tirtha river inside Brahmagiri Wildlife Sanctuary, near Gonikoppal. The 1 km forest walk to the falls passes dense shola forest; swimming is not permitted and a permit is required at the sanctuary gate.

attractions.name: Pushpagiri Wildlife Sanctuary Trek
attractions.description: A multi-day trekking area in the northern part of Kodagu district, with trails ascending to the Pushpagiri peak at 1,712 m through shola grasslands and montane forest. Permits are required and the trek demands reasonable fitness; it rewards with near-zero crowds and excellent birdwatching.

attractions.name: Chelavara Falls
attractions.description: A lesser-visited double-drop waterfall near Napoklu village, accessible via a short trail through a coffee estate. It sees far fewer tourists than Abbey Falls and the surrounding estate landscape makes for a more authentic Coorg experience; there is no formal infrastructure.

attractions.name: Omkareshwara Temple
attractions.description: A 19th-century Shiva temple in the heart of Madikeri town built in an unusual blend of Islamic and Gothic architecture with a central tank. It is genuinely singular in appearance for a Hindu temple in this region and is easy to combine with a walk through Madikeri market.
